data.hypothesis: Keep the selected parent's single-accumulator signed minimum pass and test whether unrolling the earliest-match search to eight vectors per iteration reduces loop overhead on long search prefixes. A prior single-accumulator, four-vector search measured 4.3046e-7 seconds versus 5.2559e-7 for the single-vector search, while an eight-vector search paired with a four-accumulator minimum pass measured 4.5678e-7; those results do not isolate the unroll factor. This candidate tests the eight-vector search with the single-accumulator pass, where extra eager loads could offset reduced loop overhead, particularly for inputs whose minimum occurs early.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use this as context for testing search unroll depth; the eight-vector result changed the first-pass reduction too, so it is not a clean comparison against the four-vector candidate.
memory_lessons.claim: The single-accumulator minimum pass with a four-vector equality search measured 4.3046e-7 seconds; the single-vector search with the same reduction measured 5.2559e-7. An eight-vector search paired with a four-accumulator reduction measured 4.5678e-7, so these measurements do not establish a monotonic effect from increasing search unrolling.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare this single-accumulator, eight-vector search against the four-vector variant after correctness validation; inspect random and decreasing input timings separately if available.

data.notes: The candidate retains signed AVX-512 minimum reduction, equality matching, lowest-set-lane selection, and scalar tail handling. Prior controller records show correctness on the supplied cases, but this proposed source has not been built or validated here. Controller validation should precede repeated timing comparisons; the supplied aggregate timings do not show per-pattern results.
transformations: Preserve the selected parent's single-accumulator AVX-512 signed minimum pass and scalar remainder.
Unroll the second-pass equality search across eight complete vectors per iteration and select the earliest matching vector and lowest matching lane.
Scan remaining complete vectors and the scalar tail while preserving bounds safety, first-index ties, and INT32 extrema.
